recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for stricter uniform wording across every resource-specific identifier element should be handled as a new harmonization issue, not as additional FHIR-15095 reconciliation work.
issue_request: FHIR-15095 asked that resources such as Composition, DetectedIssue, DeviceComponent, DeviceMetric, ImagingManifest, QuestionnaireResponse, SupplyRequest, and datatypes stop treating identifier as the unique logical resource id. Its Published / Persuasive with Modification resolution updated Event, Request, and Definition pattern identifier text to business-identifier wording, did not insist on 0..* cardinality everywhere, and asked editors to review resource-specific descriptions with domain-specific refinements allowed.
initial_application: Git commit 70df4285c448d78f8b09c6c7a1ff02a807e99be9, imported from SVN r13441 with subject GF#15095 - revise definitions of identifier, changed the Event, Request, and Definition pattern spreadsheets to use business-identifier wording and to add the note distinguishing business identifiers from resource identifiers.
additional_context: Current Event and Request pattern inputs retain the business-identifier wording. Definition.identifier was later revised by FHIR-40406 to align Definition pattern documentation with Canonical resources, but it still identifies the element as a business/formal identifier rather than the FHIR logical id. In source/fhir.ini, Composition, DetectedIssue, DeviceMetric, and QuestionnaireResponse are active resources; DeviceComponent is commented out, ImagingManifest is listed only in removed/legacy metadata, and SupplyRequest is not active. The active resource-specific identifier definitions either use business-identifier wording or domain-specific wording such as DeviceMetric's device/gateway/manufacturer handle identifier. Resource narrative also separately explains logical ids and business identifiers.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the original pattern-level application is present, later Definition-pattern maintenance preserves the semantic distinction, and the remaining in-build resource wording does not present identifier as the unique FHIR resource id.
